clue.text: Know-all rascal met with disaster

indicators.note: something that met with disaster is wrecked, so the letters of the two words are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who knew everything finally came to grief.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a person who irritatingly claims to know everything, which is exactly the British phrase meant.

clue.text: Maker of ropes and sails

parts.note: read as a riddle about a fibre plant whose tough leaf fibre is twisted into cordage, its name also a rearrangement of the last word

explanation.surface: A craftsman who makes rigging and canvas for ships.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ship's chandler; in fact the 'maker' is a plant fibre, and its letters also happen to rearrange the word 'sails'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is the stiff fibre of an agave plant, widely used for twine and cordage.

clue.text: Can I provide a friendly solution?

parts.note: the question 'can I' becomes 'am I able', so 'can' supplies the verb part
taken as written
the rest of the rephrased question: being able is what 'can' expresses

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help by finding a kind way out of a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can I' rephrased is 'am I able', which run together gives the word for friendly; 'solution' hints at the answer to the riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means good-natured and pleasant in manner, a close synonym for being well disposed.

clue.text: Hearing noisy neighbour could be one

definitions.meaning: a hearing in court is a legal examination of a case
a troublesome person who tries your patience is a burden in this sense

explanation.surface: A court case brought against the loud people next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is both a court hearing and, informally, an annoying person who tests one's patience.

clue.text: Record hold-ups in the timber trade

definitions.text: Record hold-ups in the timber trade

parts.words: Record hold-ups in the timber trade
parts.note: a record is a log and hold-ups are jams, and blockages of floating timber on rivers are what the phrase describes

explanation.surface: Lumber merchants suffer the worst delays ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like an adjective meaning record-breaking; it is the noun log, and jams are hold-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Logjams are tangles of floating logs blocking a river, the classic obstruction of the timber trade.

clue.text: Caught us to face this sort of sentence

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: A judge warns that being arrested means confronting a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodial sentence is one that involves imprisonment rather than a fine or probation.

clue.text: Sticks around, looking complacent

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for sticks is read backwards

parts.note: gums are glues, which stick things

explanation.surface: Someone lounges about with a self-satisfied air.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone who looks irritatingly pleased with themselves, the same as complacent.

clue.text: Bacon's lines

parts.note: looks like verses by the philosopher Francis Bacon, but means the fatty stripes running through rashers

explanation.surface: Quotations from the writings of Francis Bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaky bacon is the British name for belly bacon, with its stripes of fat and lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaks are thin lines of contrasting colour, like the fat marbling streaky bacon.

clue.text: Clue women possibly find displeasing

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged otherwise, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some women may find this crossword clue disagreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted or is disagreeable, which matches displeasing.

clue.text: Here's hoping I spring a surprise

indicators.note: used as a verb, to surprise letters is to jolt them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to catch a friend off guard with an unexpected treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I SPRING gives SPIRING, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiring means hoping or striving to achieve something, so it fits the hopeful sense.

clue.text: Puts pressure on seamen aboard

annotationWithheld.why: Puts pressure on seamen aboard (6): CREW inside SS, but 'aboard' must both supply SS and signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Going round the world is smashing opportunity for girl to take in

indicators.note: the word for girl takes in, that is contains, the shot

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
a lob in tennis is a high shot that invites the opponent to smash it

explanation.surface: A girl on a world tour gets a wonderful chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise; in tennis, a lob gives the opponent an opportunity to play a smash.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means worldwide, covering or encircling the whole planet.

clue.text: Lovely girl, outwardly competent

indicators.note: the word for competent goes on the outside, wrapping the girl's name

parts.note: able means capable or competent
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A charming young woman who looks capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and lovable, a near synonym of lovely.

clue.text: Help out with award, showing self-possession

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word are knocked out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
GM is the George Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: Someone receives a medal for assisting and shows great composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm in its old sense means calm, unexcitable temperament, so it is composure or coolness.

clue.text: Switch musical number

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
a piece is a musical number or item

explanation.surface: Swapping in a different song from a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' is not a change; it is a tress of false hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a detached lock of hair worn to add bulk, a kind of wig or toupee.

clue.text: Mischief-maker intended to limit one's credit

indicators.note: the word for intended limits, by enclosing, the next two pieces

parts.note: meant means intended
one's read as one is, I plus S
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A troublemaker meant to cap someone's borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, someone who causes trouble.

clue.text: Careless mistakes by brick carrier

parts.note: slips are small errors
a hod is a builder's trough on a pole for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A bricklayer's labourer makes sloppy errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod means done carelessly or untidily, without proper attention.

clue.text: Rouses proceedings with excruciatingly vile puns

indicators.note: the agony implied by the adverb shows the letters being twisted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dreadful wordplay perks up a dull meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To liven up a gathering is to make it more lively and animated, as rousing does.

clue.text: Cuts out aerobics without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is removed from the longer word

parts.note: aerobics are physical exercises
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone drops their keep-fit routine and stops dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut out or remove, as a surgeon excises tissue.

clue.text: Spots politician taken in by loads of money

indicators.note: the politician is taken in, held inside, by the word for loads of money

parts.note: piles means large amounts, especially of cash
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A journalist notices a politician being bribed with huge sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb meaning notices; it is the noun for skin blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimples are small inflamed spots on the skin.

clue.text: Currently it is moving between Dublin banks

definitions.text: Currently it is moving between Dublin banks

parts.words: Currently it is moving between Dublin banks
parts.note: currently suggests at present but means in a current, and banks are riverbanks rather than financial institutions

explanation.surface: Money is at the moment being transferred among Irish banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liffey is the river flowing through the centre of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liffey is the river that flows through Dublin, between its banks.

clue.text: Anticipate charge for concealing minerals

indicators.note: the word for charge hides the minerals inside itself

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Someone expects to be billed for hiding rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to see or predict in advance, which is what anticipating involves.

clue.text: Range of freshly cooked crumpets

indicators.note: cooking reworks ingredients, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A selection of crumpets straight off the griddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumpets are British griddle cakes, eaten toasted with butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a whole range or scale of related things, such as opinions.

clue.text: They support parades with conscious pride

definitions.meaning: bars or props bracing a structure
to strut is to walk in a swaggering, showy way

explanation.surface: Fans march proudly through the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Struts are structural braces, and someone who struts walks pompously to show off.

clue.text: Worker in Salvation Army appears as Father Christmas

indicators.note: the worker goes in the abbreviation for the charity

parts.note: the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A charity volunteer dresses up for the Christmas collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa, short for Santa Claus, is another name for Father Christmas.

clue.text: Conviction that can be reversed?

indicators.note: the word reads identically backwards, so reversing it changes nothing

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A guilty verdict that might be overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' looks legal, as does 'reversed'; it means a belief, and the answer reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a firmly held principle or belief, as a conviction is.

clue.text: Paid companion may show his age when confused

indicators.note: letters that are confused are mixed up, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hired escort may reveal how old a client is if he gets muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained and paid to entertain and accompany men.

clue.text: Scores goal, gaining England's final point

parts.note: a striker lands a goal, so lands means scores
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A footballer's late winner earns England the decisive point.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost tip of mainland England, in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Land's End is the far south-western extremity of England, its last point of land.

clue.text: Shorter time for teaching? That's not on

indicators.note: not on means the two letters of on are taken away

parts.note: a lesson is a period of teaching
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint about cutting class time: that is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' is British for unacceptable, which hides the removal of ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means smaller in amount, so a lesser length is shorter.

clue.text: If you want to make it you will

definitions.text: If you want to make it you will

parts.words: If you want to make it you will
parts.note: the closing word will looks like a verb but is the legal document left to heirs

explanation.surface: Determination: if you really want to achieve it, you shall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' here is a noun: one's last will and testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament, as in last will and testament, is the legal document disposing of property at death.
